newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to lower.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures called to open flat to lower Monday after choppy trade late last week, pressured by outlook of mild weather and fluctuating physical prices in the western U.S.
"It wouldn't be surprised if this thing would come off," a New York broker said.
In early over-the-counter (OTC) activity, December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were discussed at $22.75-$23.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) and December Palo Verde (PV) $21.10-$22.00.
On Friday, December COB settled at $23.58, and December PV ended at $21.75.
"It was just showing better numbers," said another New York broker, referring to a modest recovery in December COB on Friday.
The 720 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners today after being shut last Tuesday to repair a boiler tube leak.
The 428 MW coal-fired unit at the Craig power station in Colorado was also expected to return to service today after being idled Friday for maintenance.

According to the latest forecasts, the Pacific Northwest on Tuesday was predicted to enjoy seasonal temperatures in the 50s-60s Fahrenheit during the day and 30s-40s in the evening. The region would experience normal temperatures for the rest of the week.
On Tuesday, the Southwest would enjoy 70s-80s temperatures during the day and 30s-50s in the evening, and it would experience warmer-than-normal weather the remainder of the week.
